## Highlights since 0.16.19

- **Themes.** Settings › Appearance › Theme now picks a palette as well as light or dark: Lattice's own, Rosé Pine or Nord, or a `.lattice-theme.json` theme you install from a file. A theme brings its own accent, and an accent you pick yourself is adjusted to stay readable on the theme's colors.
- **Browse themes.** Settings › Appearance › Browse themes… lists themes from the Lattice theme registry, installs them in one click and offers updates. The list is signed: Lattice refuses a list that fails its signature or is older than one it has already seen, and keeps the last verified list when you're offline. If a theme is withdrawn, Lattice turns it off and says why in Settings. Themes with a known problem stay on and show a warning.
- **Plugins.** Settings › Plugins installs a plugin from a folder or a URL, and lists the permissions it asks for in plain words before you turn it on. An enabled plugin adds its commands to the command palette, and any change it makes to your bibliography is shown for you to confirm and can be undone.
- **Boards use Excalidraw.** Boards now open, edit and save as `.excalidraw` files. A `.tldr` board opens as an `.excalidraw` copy converted beside it, and the original is left as it was.
- **Project tabs come back after a restart.** After Quit or Restart, Lattice reopens each window's project tabs in their order, with the same one selected. Thanks to @knightnemo (#1094).
- **TeX updates ask for your password once.** The first TeX Live update or package install that needs your password also makes you the owner of the TeX Live folder, so later updates install without asking. Lattice now checks for updates weekly instead of daily, and MacTeX gets the same one-click update.
- **Choose where Overleaf projects download.** Open from Overleaf shows the folder a project will download into, and Choose… picks another. The next download offers the same folder again.
- **Two small settings.** Settings › Appearance › Tab style draws panel tabs filled, as before, or outlined, so you can count the open tabs at a glance. History › Compare versions has a Wrap toggle for long source lines. Thanks to @ivanvykopal for the Wrap toggle (#1120).

## Notable fixes

- In a project with more than one root document, the PDF preview reopens each document on its own page when a build switches to it, instead of the page the other one was on.
- Saving a chapter builds the root document that includes it, not the root that was built last, so a paper's section no longer compiles its rebuttal.
- A project stays linked to Overleaf after its title is renamed on Overleaf.
- Clicking into the PDF page number and leaving it unchanged no longer jumps to the top of the page.
- Selecting a very long passage no longer makes the editor stall while macOS checks it for Writing Tools. Thanks to @wchen99998 for the diagnosis (#1115).
- REVTeX's generated `<job>Notes.bib` no longer shows up in the file tree. Thanks to @ajay-mk for the fix (#1106).
- Importing files whose names are already taken asks with one row of buttons instead of a list and an Import button.
- Windows: the terminal starts in the project folder when the folder name contains brackets. Thanks to @ivanvykopal for the fix (#1023).
